text: Prepare a check list for the case mentioned below, along with the suggestions toimprove the scenario: 31% January 2006 saw a vapor cloud explosion at one of the polymerization plant, killing one worker and injuring 14 people. The accident occurred due to runaway reaction in the reactor. The Plant manufactured the product called as Acrylic Polymer in batch process. The reaction worked as a two-step process. First step is partial addition of reactant acrylic monomer and catalyst, stirring the reactor and allowing the temperature to reach desired value. Second step involved addition of remaining acrylic monomer into the reactor. The reaction is exothermic, releasing large amounts of heat. The gases from the reactor is sent through heat exchanger, condensed and sent back to the reactor. This process maintained the temperature in the reactor to the desired value. Once the plant got an order of 12% more product and the operators decided to carry out increased production in a single batch, instead of splitting the batch in two parts. It was decided that all the monomer and catalyst would be added at same time and the reactor is stirred till desired time. But as all the reactant was added together, the heat exchanger was not able to control the temperature in reactor. This lead to increase in temperature and pressure in the reactor which converted into runaway reaction. The increasing pressure caused the rupture of the rupture disc, releasing large amount of flammable mixture in to the plant. The workers heard the loud hissing sound and gathered outside the building to find out what went wrong. The workers could not open the emergency cooling water system in the plant and the minutes later there was an explosion in the plant. The building was destroyed and 14 workers were injured.

text: Investigate the following case based on Initiation, Propagation and Termination steps. List out the technical gaps in that led to accident. How could PHA if carried out before accident, saved this plant? The company ABC had plastic extrusion unit, where the raw materials were pumped to heated reactor followed by passing them to extruder where the hard plastic was converted to solid particles. During the first 15 minutes of start up the plastic considered to be unusable from reactor was diverted, before going to extruder, to 750-gallon waste tank. Steam and gases escaped through the vent on the waste tank preventing any accumulation of pressure inside. The contents of the tank were allowed to cooled down for period of hours, workers than opened the tank cover to remove the waste plastic. On the afternoon before the accident the operators begin to start up the process. But there was a mechanical failure of the extruder. The operators tried to fix the problem unsuccessfully the hot plastic continued flowing into the waste tank for unusually long time. Supervisors eventually aborted the startup but by then the waste tank has already overfilled with molten plastic. The excess plastic clogged the vent line and the emergency pressure relief line. With pressure gauge now sealed off, workers would have no reliable way to determine whether the tank was under pressure. As the outside of the waste tank gradually cooled, the hard plastic layer several inches thick formed around the inside surface of the tank but closer to the center the plastic still remained hot and molten, unknown to worker the slow decomposition reactions were occurring inside the molten plastic. Over a period of hours, the hot plastic molecules were breaking down forming gas bubbles and causing a dangerous buildup of pressure. Just after 2 AM, i.e. 12 hours after startup attempt, 3 night shift workers approached the waste tank for cleaning purpose. The workers begin to unbolt the cover of the tank. After they had removed half the number of bolts, the extreme pressure blew the 1750 pound cover of the tank with explosive force and ejected hot plastic over wide area. The waste tank recoiled backwards, breaking the hot oil pipe line creating a vapor cloud which ignited a 6 minutes’ latter. Three maintenance workers were killed instantaneously when the waste tank cover blew. This accident proves that the slow reactions that don’t produce any heat can still be hazardous. The company researchers knew that the molten plastic can react/decompose and B

Develop a layered Accident Investigation and mention the initiation, propagation and termination steps that led to accident with the help of following case study: The Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company (Goodyear) facility in Houston, Texas, witnessed a heat exchanger rupture and ammonia release accident. On June 10, 2008, Goodyear operators closed an isolation valve between the heat exchanger shell (ammonia side) and a relief valve to replace a burst rupture disk under the relief valve that provided over-pressure protection. The heat exchanger was used to cool the reactor feed. Maintenance workers replaced the rupture disk on that day; however, the closed isolation valve was not reopened. On the moming of June 11, an operator closed a biock vaive isolating the ammonia pressure control valve from the heat exchanger. The operator then connected a steam line to the process line to clean the piping. The steam flowed through the heat exchanger tubes, heated the liquid ammonia in the exchanger shell, and increased the pressure in the shell. The closed isolation and block valves prevented the increasing ammonia pressure from safely venting through either the ammonia pressure control valve or the rupture disk and relief valve. text: Develop a layered Investigation and also mention the initiation, propagation and termination steps that led to accident with the help of following case study: The Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company. (Goodyear) facility in Houston, Texas witnessed a heat exchanger rupture and ammonia release accident. On June 10, 2008 Goodyear operators closed an isolation valve between the heat exchanger shell (ammonia cooling side) and a relief valve to replace a burst rupture disk under the relief valve that provided over-pressure protection. Maintenance workers replaced the rupture disk on that day; however, the closed isolation valve was not reopened. On the morning of June 11, an operator closed a block valve isolating the ammonia pressure control valve from the heat exchanger. The operator then connected a steam line to the process line to clean the piping. The steam flowed through the heat exchanger tubes, heated the liquid ammonia in the exchanger shell, and increased the pressure in the shell. The closed isolation and block valves prevented the increasing ammonia pressure from safely venting through either the ammonia pressure control valve or the rupture disk and relief valve. The pressure in the heat exchanger shell continued climbing until it violently ruptured at about 7:30 a.m. The catastrophic rupture threw debris that struck and killed a Goodyear employee walking through the area. The rupture also released ammonia, exposing five nearby workers to the chemical. One additional worker was injured while exiting the area. Ammonia Vapor to. text: Develop a layered Accident Investigation with the help of following case study 31* January 2006 saw’a vapor cloud explosion at one of the polymerization plant killing one worker and injuring 14 people. The accident occurred due to runaway reaction in the reactor. The Plant manufactured the product called as Acrylic Polymer in batch process. The reaction worked as a two step process. First step is partial addition of reactant acrylic monomer and catalyst, stirring the reactor and allowing the temperature to reach desired value. Second step involved addition of remaining acrylic monomer into the reactor. The reaction is exothermic, releasing large amounts of heat. The gases from the reactor is sent through heat exchanger, condensed and sent back to the reactor. This process maintained the temperature in the reactor to the desired value. Once the plant got an order of 12% more product and the operators decided to carry out increased production in a single batch, instead of splitting the batch in two parts. It was decided that all the monomer and catalyst would be added at same time and the reactor is stirred till desired time. But as all the reactant was added together, the heat exchanger was not able to control the temperature in reactor. This lead to increase in temperature and pressure in the reactor } which converted into runaway reaction. The increasing pressure caused the rupture of the rupture disc, releasing large amount of flammable mixture in to the plant. The workers heard the loud hissing sound and gathered outside the building to find out what went wrong. The workers could not open the emergency cooling water system in the plant and the minutes later there was an explosion in the plant. The building was destroyed and 14 workers were injured.
